_comment: Accepted cross-platform attribute-effect findings, two kinds. DIVERGENCE ({fixture, platforms}): the control-diff verdict (active = the attribute changed the render, inert = it did not) disagrees across the platforms the attribute is declared for — semantic drift unless a deliberate platform idiom; the reason says which. UNIFORMLY-INERT ({fixture, verdict, declared}): a value the SSoT enumerates changes nothing on ANY platform — either it is the default rendering (say so in the reason) or it is dead/unimplemented everywhere. Unrecorded findings fail `jui conformance gate --cross-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and must be pruned (`jui conformance cross-effect --update`). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

android's kjui DYNAMIC renderer drops the line entirely for the object face: styled renders byte-identical to the CONTROL on android, while ios and web draw the plain line for it (byte-identical to the true face — their collapse is the recorded C2/presence-only family, value_discrimination.json). Measured on run 31068716186 artifacts, band-aware. This is NOT the presence-only shape: on android's dynamic path the presence itself is lost for the object face. The codegen path is unaffected — codegen text for true and styled is byte-identical on all three (codegen_effect.json). Owner: G (kjui dynamic). The row leaves this ledger when the android dynamic renderer draws the line for the object face; full styling stays post-release.

adjudicated host-shim limitation (web), NOT a converter defect: the emitted class is `disabled:bg-<name>`, and the conformance host resolves palette names through a GENERATED plain-CSS shim (`.bg-dark_red { … }`) that carries no variants — so the base utility renders and the `disabled:` variant has nothing to resolve to. A consumer whose globals.css registers the colours in `@theme` gets the variant from Tailwind itself. Re-measure if the host stops needing the shim. Family: host-shim-variant-gap.

contract-covered ruling filed under the wrong key: attribute_semantics.json#distribution.observable declares `View/distribution__fill` = {ios: inert, android: active, web: active} (2026-08-05 plan 49-E ruling — `fill` is SwiftUI's stack default, so ios has nothing to change). This fixture is the `common/` face of the same shape and measures the same way, but the observable names only the `View/` key, so it landed in the ledger instead of the contract. Owner: E — add the common/ face to the observable, at which point this row is stale and must be pruned in the same commit. Family: value-is-default.

measured mechanism, NOT accepted — canon question open with E. sjui blur_converter.rb hardcodes `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)` for EVERY value and derives nothing from effectStyle; the value only selects a `.preferredColorScheme` for 3 of the 9 canonical spellings (Dark / Light / ExtraLight), and the other 6 (Prominent, Regular, UltraThin, Thin, Thick, Chrome) emit nothing at all — which is why they are inert. Measured on the local ios artifacts, both lanes: `dark` differs from its control by 3,084,926 px — the WHOLE screen, because `.preferredColorScheme` is a window-level environment override and not a 100x100 blur — while `light` and `extralight` differ by exactly 0. The SSoT declares 9 canonical values with default `Regular`, so ios renders 9 declared values as at most 2 pictures. Two rulings are needed BEFORE anyone implements: (a) what each declared value maps to in SwiftUI on ios, and (b) whether the existing skinIdioms observable (Blur/effectStyle__{light,extralight} = ios inert) survives that mapping — a fix contradicts it, and a contradicted contract is a failure no ledger reason excuses. Owner: E (canon) -> B (blur_converter) + F (dynamic Blur). The 7 sibling common/effectStyle__* rows in the 51 adjudication queue are the SAME mechanism and must move with this one. Family: effectstyle-unmapped-ios.
